title: Optimization of an in vitro assay methodology for competitive binding of thyroidogenic xenobiotics with thyroxine on human transthyretin and albumin
author: Hill, Hamers, et al.
materials: The entire assay takes two days to complete for each batch of samples to be processed. The Day 1 procedure is described as follows. Prepare the solutions of the proteins, THs and competitive ligands to be used in the in vitro assay according to Table 1 and using materials specified in Table 2. First, thaw the working solutions of these components to room temperature if they have been placed in frozen storage. For the protein working solutions, prepare the day they are to be used based on the number of assay aliquots required (one vial is sufficient for approximately 45 assay samples). Take note of the protein handling recommendations in the Precautions and Tips section. Label a series of polypropylene test tubes corresponding to the samples being prepared. This should include triplicate samples for each ligand competitor concentration. steps.title: Prepare protein stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 mg human transthyretin (TTR) in 2500 µL Tris‑EDTA buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) by inversion; aliquot 40 µL into polypropylene microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C (up to 1 year). For albumin (ALB), dissolve 12.1 mg in 2500 µL Tris‑EDTA, aliquot 40 µL, and store identically. On the day of use, add 1160 µL Tris‑EDTA to each 40 µL protein aliquot and keep 25 µL per assay (final sample concentrations: 120 nM TTR, 2400 nM ALB).

steps.title: Prepare thyroid hormone stock and working mix
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 mg L‑thyroxine (T4) in 6435 µL DMSO, vortex gently, and store 1500 µL aliquots at –20 °C (up to 3 years). This yields an 11 000 nM T4 stock. Add 11 µL of this stock to 989 µL DMSO to make a 70 µL working mixture per assay containing 0.5 µL T4, 5 µL 125I‑T4 (1000 µCi · g⁻¹), and 64.5 µL Tris‑EDTA. Prepare the mixture fresh on Day 1 by pipetting 20 µL T4 working solution, 200 µL 125I‑T4 stock, and 2580 µL Tris‑EDTA into a polypropylene tube and invert to mix.

steps.title: Prepare competitor ligand solutions
steps.instruction: For T4 as competitor, create a two‑fold dilution series from 40 960 nM down to 20 nM using the 11 000 nM T4 stock; use 5 µL of each dilution per assay. For 4‑OH‑BDE‑49, dissolve 10 µg/mL in acetonitrile (97.8 % purity), perform solvent exchange to DMSO with a nitrogen evaporator, store 2000 µL aliquots in amber glass vials at 4 °C, and generate a two‑fold dilution series from 5 nM to 5120 nM, using 5 µL per assay.

steps.title: Label assay tubes and set up replicates
steps.instruction: Label a series of polypropylene test tubes for each sample, including triplicate tubes for every competitor concentration (≈45 samples per vial). Use the labeling scheme shown in Fig. 1.

steps.title: Assemble incubation mixtures
steps.instruction: For each labeled tube, pipette 5 µL of the appropriate competitor dilution (or 5 µL DMSO for control). Then add 70 µL of the T4/125I‑T4/Tris‑EDTA working mixture, followed by 25 µL of the selected protein solution (TTR or ALB). This yields a total volume of 100 µL per assay.

steps.title: Incubate and record initial radioactivity
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 300 × g for 30 s to collect liquid at the tube bottom. Measure the radioactivity of each tube on a gamma counter. Immediately cap the tubes, avoid disturbing the contents, and place them in a 4 °C refrigerator overnight to reach binding equilibrium.

steps.title: Prepare Bio‑Spin P‑6 columns
steps.instruction: Invert each Bio‑Spin® P‑6 gel column to resuspend the gel, remove the cap and tip, then centrifuge the column in a 1.5 mL tube at 1000 × g for 2 min. Discard the flow‑through (drained packing buffer).

steps.title: Load samples onto columns and separate bound ligand
steps.instruction: Using a 100 µL pipette, transfer the entire 100 µL incubation mixture from a tube to the top of the corresponding prepared column without disturbing the gel bed; release the emptied pipette tip back into the incubation tube. Repeat for all samples in the replicate set. Centrifuge the columns at 1000 × g for 4 min to elute the protein‑bound ligand.

steps.title: Measure eluate and residual radioactivity
steps.instruction: Collect the eluate fraction from each column and measure its radioactivity on the gamma counter. Also measure the residual radioactivity remaining in the original incubation tubes (which now contain the discarded pipette tips) to account for nonspecific binding and transfer loss.

steps.title: Repeat separation for remaining replicate sets (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Perform steps 5–9 for each of the other replicate sets and for each xenobiotic competitor (e.g., 4‑OH‑BDE‑49). No additional column‑rinse step is required.

steps.title: Calculate percent protein binding
steps.instruction: For each sample, compute % binding = (eluate cpm) ÷ [(Day 1 cpm) − (cpm of emptied incubation tube + pipette tip)]. Plot percent binding versus log10 competitor concentration, showing mean ± SD of triplicates. Fit curves in GraphPad Prism 7.02 using the variable‑slope inhibitor‑vs‑response equation to obtain IC50 values.

steps.title: Determine Ki values
steps.instruction: For T4, calculate Ki = IC50_T4 − [125I‑T4] (since Ki = Kd for the radioligand). For other competitors, compute Ki = IC50_competitor ÷ [1 + [125I‑T4]/Kd_T4]. Alternatively, use the simplified relation Ki_competitor = Ki_T4 ÷ (relative potency), where relative potency = IC50_T4 ÷ IC50_competitor.

steps.title: Validate assay performance
steps.instruction: Generate a duplicate calibration curve (4–2048 nM T4 for TTR, 4–1024 nM for ALB) each batch. Calibrate the gamma counter before use and include instrument blanks (empty tubes). Include positive controls (triplicate samples at the known IC50 of a potent competitor, e.g., 12.2 nM 4‑OH‑BDE‑49 for TTR) and negative controls (triplicate DMSO only). Test column performance with a sample containing Tris‑EDTA buffer instead of protein to confirm unbound ligand remains in the column. Run the entire assay twice on separate days to obtain inter‑ and intra‑day replicates (n = 6 total).
